Long recordings no longer crash Parley or get stuck on this computer, and a dropped live transcript now comes back.

**Long files import without running out of memory** (#747)

- Importing a long recording used to decode the whole file into memory first — about 1.6 GB for 2 hours and 4.6 GB for 6 hours — which could crash Parley on an 8 GB machine. It now uses a few megabytes, however long the file is.
- With Parley Cloud transcription, a file longer than 5 h 50 min is split into equal parts before anything uploads. Parley tells you right after you pick the file ("This file is long, so it will be uploaded in 2 parts") and saves each part as its own recording, "name (1/2)", "name (2/2)".
- Audio that is already Ogg/Opus is now compressed too, and a file whose format can't be compressed and is over 100 MB is refused when you pick it, with a note to convert it to MP3 or M4A.

**Live transcription comes back after it drops** (#778)

- If Parley Cloud refuses the live transcription mid-meeting (sign-in, quota, or a session limit), Parley keeps trying to reconnect for as long as the meeting records, and the meeting window says why it is waiting. Before, transcription stopped for the rest of the meeting.
- When a finished meeting's transcript has gaps, Parley re-transcribes the recording with Parley Cloud and keeps whichever transcript covers more.
- A recording that failed to reach the cloud is retried at launch, every 15 minutes and when the network comes back, not only when you open the Library.
- Recordings over 64 MB now upload in parts, so meetings longer than about 9 hours reach the cloud too.
